concerns.text: FR-003 mandates descriptors 'on log-ratio transformed composition data', but T004 computes physical descriptors 'from RAW weight percentages' with CLR used only as model input. No task delivers FR-003 as written; this is a semantic weakening the deterministic check cannot catch. Either compute descriptors per FR-003 or amend the spec explicitly.

FR-001 requires aggregation from 'Materials Project, NIST, OpenAlloy, published literature, and systematic literature review'; T001 builds the dataset exclusively from open-access literature. Constitution VI permits literature tables, so this is constitution-safe, but the database sources are silently dropped with no spec amendment or documented justification narrowing FR-001.

SC-005 specifies a threshold sweep '{low, medium, high}'; T009 defines `numpy.linspace(0.0, best_cv_r2, 11)`. The dynamic sweep arguably covers the range, but the three artifacts (spec/plan/T009) define three different sweeps; reconcile so the sensitivity analysis verifiably satisfies SC-005.

data-model.md mandates the `compositional` library for CLR and plan.md lists it as a primary dependency, but T004 instructs dropping it for an in-repo implementation 'if unavailable'. The contract/dependency docs were not updated, so contract tests and requirements.txt may still assume the rejected package — silent contract drift.

FR-011 requires sampling 'if needed' when data exceeds RAM/disk; T012 only measures usage and reports mismatches. No task implements (or explicitly rules out as unnecessary) the sampling mechanism FR-011 names. Add a statement that sampling is not triggered at this dataset scale, or a task covering it.
